reasons: Missing-clause claim is supported: p0049 (Effect of Termination) addresses only payment obligations, and no transition assistance, data return/export, or deletion-certification obligation appears in the cited text.

Redline is a pure insertion into the termination section with no alteration of existing language — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it tracks the model language closely (6 months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion thereafter).

Party and defined-term adaptation is correct (IBM as Vendor, 'Content' as the customer-data term, extension to Service Option Attachments), and survival is already secured because Section 3.5 is enumerated in the survival clause at p0169, so no additional amendment is needed.

Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90-day fallback with the same 30-day export window; deterministic checks confirm the operation applied and the transition/data-return language is present.

Minor, non-blocking drafting nuance: clause (b) conditions the 30-day return on 'Customer's request', slightly narrower than the unconditional model language, but this remains actionable and within the preferred position.
